purpose: Hall–Petch formula used to represent the contribution of grain refinement (grain boundary strengthening) to the strength of the material, computed per phase j = {RA, F}.
applicability_conditions: For polycrystalline materials under deformation; applied to phases j = {RA, F}.

symbols.meaning: contribution of grain boundary strengthening for phase j
friction stress, indicating the resistance of the global crystal lattice to dislocation movement
symbols.value: 180 MPa for RA; 100 MPa for F

symbols.meaning: Petch parameter, used to measure the relative hardening contribution of grain boundaries or phase boundaries
symbols.value: 149 MPa·μm^{1/2} for RA; 600 MPa·μm^{1/2} for F

symbols.meaning: average grain size of phase j
phase index, j = {RA, F} (RA: retained austenite)

unmapped: In the source text, the friction stress is referred to as 'r', while the equation itself uses σ_{0j} (with σ_{0RA} = 180 MPa and σ_{0F} = 100 MPa); this appears to be a typographical inconsistency.
